_comment: The known-open fleet defect floor, as a COMMITTED artifact rather than a Python literal.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (T-167, 2026-08-17). The ratchet assertions in
test_fleet_script_health.py can only run where C:/Abhay/GetWorkDone exists — on CI they
pytest.skip(). So a PR that empties the floor is validated by a CI run that CANNOT SEE the
fleet, and 'all green' means only 'the assertions did not run'. That is exactly what
happened: commit a5cde31 (2026-08-12) emptied the floor claiming 'all six T-071 findings
fixed', CI passed, and on 2026-08-17 all six still reproduced verbatim — plus a NEW
keeper-tick.cmd finding that had been invisible for five days. The gate detected the
defects and its own bookkeeping threw the signal away: the detect-then-discard class this
checker exists to catch, one level up, inside the checker.
THE CONTRACT. Every entry records the run that OBSERVED it. Shrinking the floor is a
claim about the live fleet, so it must carry evidence a reviewer can re-derive:
1. run the checker on the fleet host (see reproduce_with below),
2. remove only entries that genuinely stopped reproducing,
3. update observed_on to that run's date.
test_ratchet_floor_matches_live_fleet enforces both directions ON THE HOST. On CI, where
the fleet is absent, test_ratchet_floor_is_evidenced still runs and blocks a floor edit
whose observed_on was not refreshed — so an unevidenced shrink can no longer merge green.
RULE: entries may only be REMOVED (as the fleet lands fixes), never added to excuse a new
defect. A new defect is a red test, not a new line here.
